description:
By the around the mid 6th CE we see a cobbled platform constructed with a road leading to it from the harbour, a small community of male adults appears to have developed and were buried alongside the road leading to this feature. This has been interpreted as a monastic community developing around an early shrine. 

Sometime in the 7th CE the site was re-organised and a parallel burial community of largely adult males with signs of chronic disease and violent trauma began. These are understood to be lay burials, possibly for individuals who had come to the shrine seeking healing. At this time the burials of the monastic community moved towards the centre of the cobbled area, which appears to have become the focus of  the cult and where the earliest identified church would later be built in the 10th CE.

It is during this 7th CE re-organisation that the site appears to have become associated with St. Ethern (d. 669 CE), though there is little to suggest he had any direct connection to the site.

the community eventually left the island for Pittenweem Priory on the mainland in 1318.
